parsed.title: Electrochemical gradient ATP coupling
parsed.canonical_question: In cellular energy production, how is a concentration difference of hydrogen ions across a membrane used to synthesise adenosine triphosphate?
parsed.match_reason: The learner asks how a pH gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane is converted into chemical energy as ATP. A pH gradient is precisely a concentration difference of hydrogen ions (protons). The existing node asks how such a concentration difference across a membrane is used to synthesise ATP. The questions are semantically identical: both describe chemiosmosis — proton flow driven by the gradient through ATP synthase to produce ATP. The node summary confirms direct coverage: chemiosmosis is the use of an electrochemical gradient to drive ATP synthesis, and proton flow through ATP synthase releases the stored energy.
